text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO breach detected on continuous-batching serving path (us-west-2). Streaming p99 = 3.8s (> 2.0s SLO). Alert routed to on-call.
Maya (oncall): on it. seeing p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~3.8s for streaming endpoints. spike start ~05:43 UTC. traffic up ~1.6x.
Jordan (sre): confirming metrics — contbatch queue depth for streaming work jumped, kv-cache evictions spiked. looks correlated with a batcher packing pattern.
Devin (runtime): initial suspect: padding amplification from mixed sequence lengths + pack window letting long requests hold the batch. mix snapshot: short:long ~ 70:30, average batch size up 2.4x but effective compute dominated by longs.
Maya (oncall): customer impact? any 5xx or session drops?
Lex (prod-eng): support funnel shows elevated latency tickets for AcmeChat and Lexa-AI streaming customers. no 5xx yet, just perceived stalls.
Jordan (sre): concrete numbers from grafana:
```
sum(rate(streaming_latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le) -> p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~3.8s
contbatch_queue_depth{pool="usw2"} -> 120 (baseline 40)
kv_evictions_total increase from 10m -> 120m
```
Maya (oncall): triage checklist: 1) apply immediate mitigation to reduce tail (cap batch size / reduce pack window) 2) enable preemptive streaming shed/fairshare 3) route high-mix customers to dedicated fallback 4) longer-term: adaptive packing by seqlen.
Devin (runtime): agree. quick change I'd do: cap batcher.max_batch_size=16 (was 64), pack_window_ms=20 (was 50), enable preemptive_streaming_shed=true. will canary then roll.
Maya (oncall): please run canary to one small pool. I'll coordinate customer messaging if we see improvement.
DeployBot: Starting config update on pool canary-usw2-1: {"batcher.max_batch_size":64->16, "pack_window_ms":50->20, "preemptive_streaming_shed":false->true}
DeployBot: Config applied to canary-usw2-1.
Jordan (sre): watching canary. p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.9s within ~45s post-change. queue depth down from 120 -> 55. kv evictions trending down.
Maya (oncall): nice. patch to roll to remaining pools with staged rate 30s per pool and bump fairshare weights: schedule.weight.streaming=3, scheduler.shed_ratio=0.15.
Devin (runtime): pushing rollout command: `./infra/rollout --target=usw2 --config=contbatch-tail-mitigation-v1 --rate=30s`
DeployBot: Rollout started (usw2 pools).
Lex (prod-eng): quick ask — can we route Lexa-AI active sessions to dedicated-reserve pool for next 30m to avoid impact while we stabilize?
Maya (oncall): yes, initiating route rule for customer tag lexa-ai -> dedicated-reserve-usw2. command: `rbctl route add --customer=lexa-ai --pool=dedicated-reserve-usw2 --ttl=1800s`
DeployBot: Route rule created. sessions will drain to fallback pool within 90s.
Jordan (sre): monitoring across all pools: p99 now ~1.6-2.0s across rolled nodes. overall request success rate unchanged. no new 5xx.
Devin (runtime): logging note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = mixed-seqlen padding amplification + pack-window too permissive allowing long sequences to enlarge batches; fairness scheduling allowed some tenants to monopolize. adding an adaptive packer and seqlen-aware bucketing to roadmap.
Maya (oncall): customer impact summary for ops: AcmeChat — elevated UX latency, incidents open with support but no data loss; Lexa-AI routed to dedicated pool, mitigating further impact. No SLO violations now for >5m; will keep pager open until stable 15m window.
Jordan (sre): oncall handoff plan: I'll stay until stable, @Maya please note for next shift. create follow-up ticket for: 1) adaptive packing PoC 2) fairshare tuning defaults 3) alert noise tweak (p99 sustained >2.0s for 5m).
Maya (oncall): ack. creating ticket and adding triage items.
DeployBot: Rollout completed for all targeted pools in us-west-2.
Jordan (sre): alert cleared (automated): p99 < 2.0s sustained 10m. closing paging sequence unless escalation.
Maya (oncall): thumbs. we should notify affected customers with mitigation summary. I'll draft comms.
Lex (prod-eng): thanks team — can we include suggested customer-side best practice: cap streaming session max tokens and use shorter chunking to avoid long-run jobs?
Devin (runtime): noted. adding to postmortem.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved (mitigation applied, rollout complete).
Maya (oncall): closing thread once postmortem created. good job everyone :thumbsup:
